item.title: "This should be a head-down moment."
item.description: Vice President Kamala Harris is campaigning for Dems ahead of the midterms, and was asked directly: is she running for president again in 2028? Scott Galloway and Jessica Tarlov discuss, on Raging Moderates.
item.content:encoded:
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/SD-5n20SBOM

Transcript

Are you running for president? >> Oh, girl, come on. >> [laughter] >> We have to know this. You know the people want to know. Are we going to get another moment to see >> decided. I haven't decided yet. I will. I promise. >> These guys playing the reluctant bride, I think it's a bad look. If they want to say, I want to see if I get enough support, but if I have enough support, I'll run, that would at least be a more honest answer. But if there's anything resembling an opening, these people are all in. None of them are going to say, "Yeah, I'm polling number one, but I sat down with my family and we decided to kind of take it easy this

>> You will never hear that. >> It does complicate the swirl around the race and our chances in the midterms. And I'm glad to see that she's going on the campaign trail, and I'm sure she will be very useful to the candidates who she is stumping with, especially with core demographics. I generally feel like this should be a head-down moment, not a chitchat moment. And I think that it just creates these side shows when there are tight races all over the country, where there are candidates who have no business being close or even slightly ahead in ruby-red places, where

Joe Biden and Kamala Harris are not particularly popular. And people don't want to be reminded that actually you are part of that team.
